sections.html:
On the Mississippi side of the state line, Southaven is a DeSoto County city roughly 14 miles south of downtown Memphis. As a principal city of Greater Memphis, it has many owners who work, shop and fly out of Tennessee yet pay their taxes in Mississippi. The 2020 census counted 54,648 residents, and the 2024 estimate of 57,493 makes it the third largest city in the state and the largest Memphis suburb.

The city covers about 41.5 square miles. Interstate 55, which also carries the I-69 designation, runs north to south through it, with U.S. 51 and Mississippi Highway 302 as other main roads. Memphis International Airport is about two miles north of the city's center point, and flight paths from both north-south runways lead directly over town, so buyers sometimes ask about noise.

Southaven began as residential subdivisions and was incorporated in 1980. Memphis homebuilder Kemmons Wilson planned subdivisions of small starter homes just over the state line, and the city then doubled its land area while its population tripled. Houses built in different decades carry different repair needs, and a seller usually hears about them from the buyer's inspection report. A house that struggles through inspection is where an as-is cash sale often comes up.

Hot summers, steady rain and storm damage put roofs and drainage at the top of most inspection reports. Nearly 55 inches of rain fall in a year, with April the wettest month, and an EF-2 tornado touched down in Southaven on February 5, 2008.

  • Roofs: look for lifted shingles and granule loss after storm seasons.
  • Drainage: standing water near the slab or crawl space often shows up in inspections.
  • HVAC: long cooling seasons put heavy wear on air conditioners.

Plenty of Southaven households have a Tennessee job, doctor or school connection. When you sell, remember that the house, the tax bill and the deed are all in Mississippi, so Mississippi rules apply even if your agent, lawyer or lender is across the line. Confirm that whoever handles your closing is comfortable with DeSoto County recording and tax practices.

The county mails the bill. It covers the preceding assessment year and falls due February 1, with the next Monday accepted without penalty or interest when the first lands on a weekend or holiday.

Assessments follow a state formula: 10 percent of true value for a house its owner lives in, 15 percent for other real property such as a rental. County, city and school district each set a millage rate, and all three apply to the assessed value. A bigger bill can come from a higher value, a higher rate, or both.

  • Pay in person at the Tax Collector's offices in Hernando, Olive Branch or Horn Lake, by mail, or online.
  • The DeSoto County Tax Collector's number is 662-469-8030.
  • The county holds its tax sale on the last Monday in August, using an online bidding platform run with GovEase.

A tax sale on a house you are trying to sell clouds the title and usually has to be cleared before closing. Ask the DeSoto office how redemption works on your parcel before you rely on it.

Anyone who disagrees with an assessment can ask for a hearing with the Board of Supervisors, normally by the first Monday in August before the tax is due. Contact the Chancery Clerk for the process.

Your exemption stays with you. The next owner has to file with the county Tax Assessor from January 1 to April 1, because it is never automatic. The applicant must own and occupy the house as a primary residence on January 1, with the deed filed at the Chancery Clerk before January 7. A buyer who closes in spring will likely wait until the next tax year, while one who closed in December can apply in time.

A missed filing or an income tax problem can cost the exemption. A seller who also owns a second house should check that only one property carries it.

Southaven's Building Department issues permits and examines plans, and its phone number is 662-393-4639. A homeowner may submit the building permit for their own home but must hire a contractor holding a Mississippi state license for trade work.

If you started a project and stopped, ask the Building Department whether anything is still open before you list or accept an offer. Unfinished permitted work can stall a sale.

Southaven owners can pick an agent, a sale by owner, or a cash buyer, and each fits a different situation. A listing makes sense for a house in good order when you can wait through showings and the buyer's financing. A sale by owner keeps the commission in your pocket but leaves every form and negotiation on your desk. A cash buyer is the quickest and asks for no repairs.

If the buyer's inspector finds problems, you will either lower the price, pay for repairs or lose the buyer. A direct as-is sale takes that step away. Ask any buyer to put the offer in writing, and keep the paperwork you have been given.

Mississippi Code section 89-1-503 obliges the seller to deliver the written property condition disclosure statement ahead of the title transfer. If the statement comes after an offer, the buyer can cancel within three days of hand delivery or five of mailing.

A cash purchase as is does not remove that duty. It changes who pays for the repairs. Cash Home Buyers works with Southaven sellers who would rather sell the house in its present condition than manage contractors, and we explain the terms in writing before anyone commits.

A sale of this kind still follows the usual path. A title search finds liens and unpaid taxes, those are paid from your proceeds, you sign the deed, and the Chancery Clerk records it. Bring photo identification, tax receipts, permit records and any payoff figure for a mortgage. Because no lender is involved on the buyer's side, the appraisal and loan approval stages do not slow the date.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Southaven, MS without making repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Mississippi does not require repairs before sale, but you must give the buyer the written property condition disclosure statement. Buyers who purchase as is account for repairs in what they pay.

faqs.q: When are DeSoto County property taxes due?
faqs.a: By February 1 for the preceding assessment year, with a grace period to the following Monday if that date falls on a weekend or holiday.

faqs.q: When does DeSoto County hold its tax sale?
faqs.a: On the last Monday in August each year, through an online bidding platform.

faqs.q: Does the buyer keep my homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. A buyer must apply on their own between January 1 and April 1, and must own and occupy the home on January 1 of the tax year.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a building permit in Southaven?
faqs.a: The Building Department at 662-393-4639. A homeowner may submit the permit for their own home, but trade work needs a contractor with a Mississippi state license.
